introduction.en: Searching algorithms are fundamental techniques used to find a specific element or determine its position within a data structure. Efficient searching is crucial for building fast applications and is one of the most frequently tested topics in coding interviews.
introduction.hi: Searching algorithms wo basic techniques hain jo kisi data structure mein ek specific element dhundhne ya uski position pata karne ke liye use hoti hain. Efficient searching fast applications banane ke liye bahut zaroori hai aur ye coding interviews mein sabse zyada puche jaane wale topics mein se ek hai.

realLifeAnalogy.en: Think of searching like finding a word in a dictionary. If you go page by page from the start, that's Linear Search - slow but works on any book. If you open the middle, check if your word comes before or after, and keep halving - that's Binary Search - much faster but the dictionary must be sorted!
realLifeAnalogy.hi: Searching ko aise samjho jaise dictionary mein ek word dhundhna. Agar tum pehle page se ek ek page dekhte jao, wo Linear Search hai - slow hai par kisi bhi book pe kaam karega. Agar tum beech mein kholo, dekho word pehle aata hai ya baad mein, aur aadha aadha karte jao - wo Binary Search hai - bahut fast hai par dictionary sorted honi chahiye!

content.en:
Linear Search is the simplest searching algorithm. It checks each element one by one from the beginning until the target element is found or the array ends.

**Key Properties:**
- Works on both sorted and unsorted arrays
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- No preprocessing required
- Best for small datasets or unsorted data

**When to use Linear Search:**
- Array is unsorted
- Array is very small
- You need to search only once
- Data structure doesn't support random access (like linked lists)
content.hi:
Linear Search sabse simple searching algorithm hai. Ye shuruaat se ek ek element check karta hai jab tak target element mil nahi jaata ya array khatam nahi ho jaata.

**Important Baatein:**
- Sorted aur unsorted dono arrays pe kaam karta hai
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Koi preprocessing nahi chahiye
- Chhote datasets ya unsorted data ke liye best hai

**Linear Search kab use karein:**
- Array sorted nahi hai
- Array bahut chhota hai
- Sirf ek baar search karna hai
- Data structure random access support nahi karta (jaise linked lists)

keyPoints.en: Linear Search works on unsorted arrays - no sorting needed
keyPoints.hi: Linear Search unsorted arrays pe kaam karta hai - sorting ki zaroorat nahi

keyPoints.en: Time Complexity is O(n) - in worst case, checks every element
keyPoints.hi: Time Complexity O(n) hai - worst case mein har element check karna padta hai

keyPoints.en: Best case is O(1) when element is at the first position
keyPoints.hi: Best case O(1) hai jab element pehli position pe ho

content.en:
Binary Search is a highly efficient algorithm that works on **sorted arrays**. It repeatedly divides the search space in half by comparing the target with the middle element.

**Key Properties:**
- Array MUST be sorted
- Time Complexity: O(log n)
- Divides search space by half each time
- Two approaches: Iterative and Recursive

**How it works:**
1. Find the middle element
2. If middle == target, return the index
3. If target < middle, search in the left half
4. If target > middle, search in the right half
5. Repeat until found or search space is empty
content.hi:
Binary Search ek bahut efficient algorithm hai jo **sorted arrays** pe kaam karta hai. Ye baar baar search space ko aadha karta hai target ko middle element se compare karke.

**Important Baatein:**
- Array SORTED hona chahiye
- Time Complexity: O(log n)
- Har baar search space aadhi ho jaati hai
- Do tarike hain: Iterative aur Recursive

**Kaise kaam karta hai:**
1. Middle element dhundho
2. Agar middle == target, index return karo
3. Agar target < middle, left half mein dhundho
4. Agar target > middle, right half mein dhundho
5. Jab tak mile ya search space khatam ho jaaye

keyPoints.en: Array MUST be sorted for Binary Search to work
keyPoints.hi: Binary Search ke liye array SORTED hona zaroori hai

keyPoints.en: Use mid = low + (high - low) / 2 to avoid integer overflow
keyPoints.hi: Integer overflow se bachne ke liye mid = low + (high - low) / 2 use karo

keyPoints.en: O(log n) is exponentially faster than O(n) for large arrays
keyPoints.hi: Bade arrays ke liye O(log n), O(n) se bohot zyada fast hai

content.en:
A rotated sorted array is a sorted array that has been rotated at some pivot point. For example, [4, 5, 6, 7, 0, 1, 2] is a rotation of [0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7].

**Key Insight:** Even after rotation, at least one half of the array (left or right of mid) is always sorted. We can use this property to apply a modified binary search.

**Algorithm:**
1. Find mid element
2. Determine which half is sorted
3. Check if target lies in the sorted half
4. If yes, search in sorted half; else search in the other half

**Why it works:**
- If left half is sorted (arr[low] <= arr[mid]), we can easily check if target is in [low, mid]
- If right half is sorted (arr[mid] <= arr[high]), we can check if target is in [mid, high]
content.hi:
Rotated sorted array ek sorted array hai jo kisi pivot point pe rotate ho gaya hai. Jaise [4, 5, 6, 7, 0, 1, 2] ye [0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7] ka rotation hai.

**Key Insight:** Rotation ke baad bhi, array ka kam se kam ek half (mid ke left ya right) hamesha sorted rehta hai. Hum is property ko use karke modified binary search laga sakte hain.

**Algorithm:**
1. Mid element dhundho
2. Pata karo konsa half sorted hai
3. Check karo target sorted half mein hai ya nahi
4. Agar haan, sorted half mein dhundho; nahi toh doosre half mein dhundho

**Ye kyun kaam karta hai:**
- Agar left half sorted hai (arr[low] <= arr[mid]), toh easily check kar sakte hain target [low, mid] mein hai ya nahi
- Agar right half sorted hai (arr[mid] <= arr[high]), toh check kar sakte hain target [mid, high] mein hai ya nahi

keyPoints.en: At least one half is always sorted in a rotated sorted array
keyPoints.hi: Rotated sorted array mein kam se kam ek half hamesha sorted rehta hai

keyPoints.en: Use the sorted half to decide which direction to search
keyPoints.hi: Sorted half use karo ye decide karne ke liye ki kis direction mein search karna hai

keyPoints.en: Time Complexity remains O(log n) - same as regular binary search
keyPoints.hi: Time Complexity O(log n) hi rehti hai - regular binary search jaisi

content.en:
Searching in a 2D matrix that is sorted row-wise and column-wise can be done efficiently using the **Staircase Search** approach.

**Matrix Properties:**
- Each row is sorted left to right
- Each column is sorted top to bottom
- First element of each row is greater than the last element of previous row (for fully sorted matrix)

**Staircase Search (Row-wise & Column-wise sorted):**
1. Start from top-right corner (or bottom-left)
2. If current element == target, found!
3. If current element > target, move left (eliminate column)
4. If current element < target, move down (eliminate row)

**Binary Search approach (Fully sorted matrix):**
- Treat the 2D matrix as a 1D sorted array
- Map index: row = mid / cols, col = mid % cols
- Apply standard binary search
content.hi:
2D matrix jisme rows aur columns dono sorted hain, usme efficiently search karne ke liye **Staircase Search** approach use hoti hai.

**Matrix ki Properties:**
- Har row left se right sorted hai
- Har column top se bottom sorted hai
- Har row ka pehla element pichli row ke last element se bada hai (fully sorted matrix mein)

**Staircase Search (Row-wise & Column-wise sorted):**
1. Top-right corner se start karo (ya bottom-left se)
2. Agar current element == target, mil gaya!
3. Agar current element > target, left jao (column eliminate)
4. Agar current element < target, neeche jao (row eliminate)

**Binary Search approach (Fully sorted matrix):**
- 2D matrix ko 1D sorted array ki tarah treat karo
- Index map karo: row = mid / cols, col = mid % cols
- Standard binary search lagao

keyPoints.en: Staircase search starts from top-right or bottom-left corner
keyPoints.hi: Staircase search top-right ya bottom-left corner se start hoti hai

keyPoints.en: Each step eliminates one row or one column - O(m + n) complexity
keyPoints.hi: Har step mein ek row ya ek column eliminate hoti hai - O(m + n) complexity

keyPoints.en: For fully sorted matrix (row-major order), use Binary Search for O(log(m*n))
keyPoints.hi: Fully sorted matrix (row-major order) ke liye Binary Search use karo O(log(m*n)) ke liye
